summary: Martinez sits at the head of the Carquinez Strait, which means the county seat of Contra Costa County doubles as a genuine waterfront town — not a bay-visible-from-a-hilltop town, but one where the downtown marina and shoreline park put you at the edge of tidal water flowing between the Sacramento River Delta and San Francisco Bay. That geography also delivers a distinctive microclimate: average highs hover around 70°F with 9.3 hours of daily sunshine, but summer afternoons can spike well above that before marine air funnels through the strait and drops evening temps toward 50°F — a natural air conditioner that neighboring inland valleys don't enjoy. The compact downtown, anchored along a few walkable blocks near the waterfront, holds independent restaurants, coffee shops, and a weekly farmers' market, giving the city a small-town Main Street rhythm despite sitting roughly 35 miles northeast of San Francisco. Major employers lean heavily on county government offices headquartered here and the nearby Shell Martinez Refinery, one of the oldest refineries on the West Coast, so this is partly a job center and partly a commuter base feeding BART-connected stations in Pleasant Hill and Concord. Housing math is tight but not absurd by Bay Area standards: at a median income of $125,436 against an $824,700 median home price, the price-to-income ratio lands around 6.6 — stretched, yet meaningfully below the ratios in closer-in East Bay cities. The surrounding hills and ridgelines channel views toward Mount Diablo to the southeast and open water to the north, and regional trails connecting to the broader East Bay park system sit within a short drive. Martinez functions as a place where county-seat infrastructure and strait-side geography create a texture that's distinctly its own, though the tradeoff is that stepping outside its small downtown core quickly shifts the feel toward car-dependent suburbia.
